The page derives F_q^+R_beta=R_beta^{-1}F_q^+ by substitution, tensors it to RF_s^+R=F_s^+, uses that permutations commute with pointwise products, and then applies the convolution rule and F^+F=I/S. This is the paper's argument, and the conjugation remark for RF_s^+ is included.
'Substituting w'=beta w gives (1/q)sum z_{w'}e^{2pi i w' beta^{-1} j/q}=(R_beta^{-1}F_q^+z)_j'. This is correct and is the paper's h=ck substitution, renamed.
'Each t_i is a unit modulo s_i and R applies R_{t_i} on axis i, so tensoring gives RF_s^+R=F_s^+'. The intermediate F_s^+R=R^{-1}F_s^+ is left implicit, but the step is immediate.
The convolution rule F_s(u*v)=S(F_su).(F_sv) is asserted, as in the paper. F_s^+F_s=I/S is obtained by tensoring the asserted F_q^+F_q=I/q.
'so this equals (1/S)F_s^+F_s(u*v)=u*v/S^2', combining the two normalizations exactly as the paper does.

errors.quote: Both maps are applied one line at a time, so errors and times add over the d axes: error below $dp^2$
errors.problem: The per-axis error p^2 is never given on the page, because the one-axis statement omits 'error less than p^2'. The reason given is also not the paper's. In the paper, each axis map is a contraction whose error is the maximum, not the sum, of its line errors (< p^2), and composing the d contraction axis maps adds the errors to < dp^2. Line-by-line application is not what makes errors add.

errors.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$.
errors.problem: The paper chooses distinct odd primes s_i, so that gcd(s_i,t_i)=1 (Lemma hypothesis) and 'each t_i is a unit modulo s_i', which the page later uses. As written, s_i=2 is allowed, and then t_i is not a unit modulo s_i.

errors.quote: where $*$ is the [cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$
errors.problem: In the chirp identity, * is the cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups Z/t_1 x ... x Z/t_d: it is d-dimensional and a has period t_i in coordinate i. Since every t_i is a power of two, this group is not cyclic of order T, so it is not a one-dimensional convolution of length T.
